title_en: Dispute over Child Support for Children Conceived by Artificial Insemination
keywords_en: civil; marriage and family dispute; child custody dispute; first instance; basic people's court; natural person; Marriage Law; legal status of children conceived through artificial insemination; duty of child support after divorce; in favor of plaintiff; artificial insemination; divorce; child custody; marriage; dispute over custody of children conceived through artificial insemination
full_text_en:
A v. B — Dispute over Child Support for a Child Conceived through Artificial Insemination

Plaintiff: Ms. A.

Defendant: Mr. B.

Plaintiff Ms. A filed a lawsuit with a basic people's court regarding a dispute over marriage and child support with Defendant Mr. B.

Plaintiff's Allegations: After marriage, the parties had a poor relationship and frequently quarreled. The defendant never showed concern for me or my family, resulting in the complete breakdown of the marital relationship. I now request a divorce; the child shall be placed under my custody, with the defendant bearing child support expenses; property located at each party's residence shall be owned separately.

Defendant's Defense: Although the marital relationship has broken down, reconciliation is preferable. If the plaintiff insists on divorce, I agree. The child was conceived through artificial insemination performed without my consent, and has no blood relation to me. If the child is raised and educated by me, I am willing to bear child support expenses; if the child is raised by the plaintiff, I will not bear child support expenses. I agree with the plaintiff's opinion on property division.

Facts Found by the Court (at closed trial): Plaintiff Ms. A and Defendant Mr. B married in July 1978. After years of infertility, hospital examination revealed that Mr. B was infertile. In the second half of 1984, the couple, through acquaintances, arranged for Ms. A to undergo two artificial insemination procedures at the hospital, both unsuccessful. In early 1985, the couple went to the hospital again and Ms. A underwent three more artificial insemination procedures. Shortly thereafter, Ms. A became pregnant and gave birth to a son in January 1986. Subsequently, the couple frequently quarreled over trivial household matters, lived separately for a long period, and their marital relationship broke down.

Opinion of the Court: The marital relationship between Plaintiff Ms. A and Defendant Mr. B has indeed completely broken down. After court mediation, both parties agreed to divorce. Pursuant to Article 25 of the Marriage Law of the People's Republic of China, the divorce shall be granted. The son born during the marriage was conceived through artificial insemination without the parties having gone through formal written consent procedures. At the time of the artificial insemination procedures, Mr. B was present and did not raise any objection or dissenting opinion; for the ten years following the child's birth, Mr. B treated the child as his own biological child in raising and educating him, and even after the couple quarreled and lived separately without contact, Mr. B continued to send child support payments. The Supreme People's Court, in its *Reply on the Legal Status of Children Born Through Artificial Insemination During the Marriage Relationship* dated July 8, 1991, clearly stated: "A child born through artificial insemination with the mutual consent of both parties during the marriage relationship shall be regarded as the legitimate child of the husband and wife, and the rights and duties between parents and child shall be governed by the relevant provisions of the Marriage Law." In accordance with the legislative intent of the Marriage Law and the provisions of the Supreme People's Court's Reply, the child born during the marriage of Ms. A and Mr. B shall be regarded as the legitimate child of both parties. Mr. B's current denial of his consent to Ms. A's artificial insemination procedures, and his refusal on that basis to bear child support obligations, is unfounded. Pursuant to Articles 15 and 29 of the Marriage Law, regardless of which parent the child lives with, both parents have the duty to raise and educate the child. According to Article 5 of the Supreme People's Court's *Several Specific Opinions on the Handling of Child Support Issues in Divorce Cases by People's Courts*, which provides: "Where the parents dispute whether a minor child aged ten or above should live with the father or the mother, the child's opinion shall be considered," the court solicited the child's opinion, and the child expressed a willingness to live with the mother; this shall be granted. Pursuant to Article 31 of the Marriage Law, both parties have agreed on the division of community property through consultation, and the court shall not intervene. Accordingly, this People's Court rendered judgment on July 15, 1996:

1. The divorce of Plaintiff Ms. A and Defendant Mr. B is granted.
2. The child shall be raised and educated by Plaintiff Ms. A. Defendant Mr. B shall pay child support in the amount of RMB 130 per month from July 1996 until the child becomes financially independent.
3. There is no dispute between the parties on property division.

After the judgment was announced, neither Ms. A nor Mr. B filed an appeal.
